title: End-to-end R&D architecture for epidemic countermeasures
bottleneck: Epidemic R&D is a fragmentary, supply-driven pipeline geared to market opportunities rather than public health need: one-off partnerships develop countermeasures for whichever pathogen attracts attention, then dissolve. There is no standing, publicly directed portfolio covering development, registration, manufacturing, and equitable deployment.
why_it_blocks: Without an end-to-end architecture, each outbreak restarts the same scramble, and countermeasures for diseases of low-income populations never get developed at all. Preparedness stays performative.
current_state: CEPI and similar bodies fund prototype vaccines for priority pathogens, but the WHO pandemic agreement's financing and coordination mechanisms remain unratified. The R&D ecosystem still relies primarily on private-sector incentives. The 100 Days Mission sets a concrete target for countermeasures within 100 days of a threat, but without pre-negotiated manufacturing and liability frameworks, rapid development still stalls at deployment.
